html:
The Kamilaroi, or Gamilaraay, are an Aboriginal Australian people whose Country runs across the plains and slopes of northern New South Wales into southern Queensland. They are one of the four largest Indigenous nations in Australia. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Their land is drained by the Namoi, Gwydir and Barwon rivers, which feed the Darling. People fished, hunted kangaroo and emu, and gathered seeds and roots. Their language belongs to the large Pama-Nyungan family. Neighbours included the Wiradjuri to the south, the Wailwan to the west and the Bigambul to the north.

British stockmen pushed onto their land in the 1820s and 1830s, and fighting followed. In 1838 mounted police killed many Kamilaroi at Waterloo Creek, and stockmen murdered Wirrayaraay people, a Kamilaroi group, at Myall Creek. Seven of the Myall Creek killers were hanged, a rare case of colonists punished for killing Aboriginal people. Gamilaraay is now taught again in schools. Their wider story is told under Aboriginal Australian societies.
